@nexxeln #42274 uses UTF-16LE `-EncodedCommand` for `.cmd`/`.bat` PowerShell wrappers and keeps `-Command` for direct executables. The portable tests passed in earlier validation, but I haven't run the native Windows case.

The blocked workflow has a Windows unit job, and the PR includes a real `pwsh.cmd` regression. Could you enable CI so we can check it? The test needs `pwsh` or `powershell` installed to exercise that path.

@nexxeln #42063 prevents an empty compaction summary from becoming the history boundary. V1 still accepts a finished, error-free summary without checking for text; Core/V2 handles empty text separately. The PR has regression coverage and no conflicts, but code CI is waiting for approval. Could you review that guard and enable the checks?

@rekram1-node #43675 covers children created during the run, but its thread reports a remaining hang when `task_id` reuses an earlier child and no `session.created` event fires. I'd narrow #42310 to that case: keep the merged event tracking and follow `parentID` only when the child isn't already known. Unrelated sessions would still stay outside the approval tree.

Would that be a useful scope for this PR?

@jlongster I need to narrow the explanation in #42176: the compaction call already stops, but a non-overflow halt leaves the saved assistant message without `finish`. `MessageV2.latest` uses that field to decide which tasks are still pending.

Is `finish: error` the right terminal state here? The one-line change has a direct halt assertion.

@kitlangton #42316 hides compaction-owned parts and synthetic continuation text without changing the JSONL schema. I noticed that its guards also affect normal text output. Should this fix apply only to JSONL, or should both modes hide those internal messages?

Once that's settled, I can resolve the #43675 overlap while keeping descendant permission tracking and add a focused mocked-compaction output test.

@jlongster #42303 keeps the unterminated-JSON diagnosis qualified: arguments may have been truncated, and the original parse error is preserved. It also keeps the internal repair tool out of provider requests. The change improves the diagnosis; it doesn't fix transport-size limits.

The branch has no conflicts and has focused regression coverage. Could you enable code CI and review that diagnostic change?

@nexxeln #42317 puts the selected agent's name in the existing environment block, alongside the model and working directory. It updates the sole caller and includes built-in/custom-agent tests.

The PR has no conflicts, but its test/typecheck workflows are waiting for approval. Could you enable them and review whether this is the right place to provide agent identity?

Not a duplicate of either, as far as I can tell. #40955 and #48175 are both about the queue misbehaving when it exists (messages dropped on interrupt, prompt_async racing a tool call). This one is a level below that: in the app client the queue cannot exist at all. `settings.general.followup()` is coerced to `"steer"` in three places (`settings.tsx` L353-356, L372-375, L376-378), so `queueEnabled` in `session.tsx` is permanently false and the `shouldQueue` branch in `submit.ts` is dead code. Fixing those two would not fix this; restoring the queue path would. Happy to close this in favor of #44108 if maintainers prefer one tracking issue for the app-side queue removal, though.

Adding another concrete use case: I run one OpenCode server with many parallel sessions. When an agent needs its instructions or agent documentation updated, the current restart requirement creates a bad choice: wait for every active task to finish, or interrupt all sessions to make the update available.

A hot reload of agent/instruction documentation—ideally file-watched, or through a narrowly scoped reload command/API—would let new work see the updated docs without disturbing in-flight tasks. This is especially important for agent-driven workflows where agents need to improve their own operating documentation as the work evolves.

Confirmed — the workaround works. After nesting `reasoningEffort` under `settings.providerOptions` for each variant (and restarting the service), streamed `reasoning_content` is now persisted as `reasoning` parts on assistant messages; before the change the session had 0 reasoning parts across ~500 assistant messages.

One suggestion alongside the flatten fix: the hardest part of debugging this was that `settings.reasoningEffort` was silently ignored — the request body was correct, the server streamed `reasoning_content`, yet nothing surfaced and no warning was logged. A debug-level log (or config validation error) for unrecognized keys under `variants[].settings` would have shortened this to minutes. Until the flattened shape lands, it may also be worth a note in the variants docs that the `@opencode/ai/providers/openai-compatible` package currently requires the `providerOptions` nesting.

I encountered the same effect today: opencode edited files via bash while in plan mode. I think this possibility / lack of hard safeguards should at least me mentioned in the documentation. Right now there is:

http://opencode.ai/docs

> OpenCode has a Plan mode that disables its ability to make changes and instead suggest how it’ll implement the feature.

http://opencode.ai/docs/agents/

> [Use plan](http://opencode.ai/docs/agents/#use-plan)
> 
> Mode: primary
> 
> A restricted agent designed for planning and analysis. We use a permission system to give you more control and prevent unintended changes. By default, all of the following are set to ask:
> 
> * file edits: All writes, patches, and edits
> * bash: All bash commands
>
